questions.title: Aircraft drops a parcel — projectile time & speed

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Draw a curved path from the aircraft to the ground: it starts horizontal at the aircraft (the parcel's initial velocity is the horizontal 42 m s⁻¹) and curves downwards, with the gradient (slope) becoming increasingly steep as the vertical speed increases towards the ground.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Vertical motion: s = ut + ½at², with u = 0 and s = 63 m:
63 = ½ × 9.81 × t²
t = √(2 × 63 / 9.81) = 3.6 s

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
The horizontal component of velocity is unchanged at 42 m s⁻¹; the vertical component is 35 m s⁻¹ from (b)(iii):
speed² = 35² + 42²
speed = √2989 = 55 m s⁻¹

questions.title: Collision of two balls — momentum, kinetic energy & force

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The total momentum of a system of bodies is constant (total momentum before = total momentum after), provided that no resultant external force acts on the system (i.e. the system is isolated).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
By conservation of momentum (taking the direction of ball X's motion as positive):
240 × 16 = 480 × v
v = 3840 / 480 = 8.0 m s⁻¹ ✓

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
KE before = ½mv² = ½ × 0.24 × 16² = 30.7 J
KE after = ½ × 0.48 × 8.0² = 15.4 J
ΔEK = 30.7 − 15.4 = 15 J (a decrease, so the collision is inelastic)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
F = Δp/Δt = (0.24 × 16) / (2.0 × 10⁻³)
F = 3.84 / 2.0×10⁻³ = 1900 N
direction: to the left (opposite to ball X's motion — it is brought to rest)

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: By Newton's third law, the force exerted on ball Y by ball X has the same magnitude (1900 N) and is opposite in direction (to the right) to the force exerted on ball X by ball Y.

questions.title: Beam with immersed cylinder — moments & upthrust

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: For a system in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a point equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Taking moments about the pivot:
anticlockwise moment of the load: 2.6 × 0.40
clockwise moment of the cylinder: the cylinder's effective downward force on the beam is (4.0 − U), at distance 0.40 m:
2.6 × 0.40 = (4.0 − U) × 0.40
U = 4.0 − 2.6 = 1.4 N ✓

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
U = ρgV, with V = Ah for the immersed volume:
U = ρgAh
A = U/(hρg) = 1.4 / (0.10 × 1.0×10³ × 9.81)
A = 1.4×10⁻³ m²

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Sketch a straight line of constant negative gradient, starting at (0.10, 0.40) and ending at (0.29, 0). (As h increases, the upthrust U = ρgAh increases, so the cylinder's effective downward force (4.0 − U) on the beam decreases; equilibrium then requires x to decrease linearly until x = 0, when U = 4.0 N at h = 4.0/(ρgA) ≈ 0.29 m.)

questions.title: Two wires supporting a load — Young modulus

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Stress is the (normal) force per unit cross-sectional area.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Strain is the extension per unit unstretched length.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
The load is suspended midway between the two wires, so each wire supports 9.0 N.
E = FL/Ax → A = FL/(Ex)
A = (9.0 × 0.84) / (1.9×10⁹ × 0.47×10⁻³)
A = 8.5×10⁻⁶ m²

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Both wires support the same load F with the same unstretched length L and the same extension x, so the strain is the same in both wires and the stress is smaller in Y because its cross-sectional area is greater (stress = F/A). Since Young modulus = stress/strain, the Young modulus of wire Y is less than 1.9×10⁹ Pa.

questions.title: String stationary wave & rotating-source Doppler effect

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Mark a cross labelled N at a node — X or Y, or a point 0.16 m (λ/2) from an end where the string has zero displacement — and a cross labelled A at an antinode — a point of maximum displacement (a peak or trough of the wave pattern, e.g. the centre of the string).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
The stationary wave shows 1.5 wavelengths between X and Y (three half-wavelengths):
1.5λ = 0.48 m
λ = 0.48 × (2/3) = 0.32 m ✓

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
The maximum frequency is detected when the source moves directly towards the observer (so the observed frequency is f₀ = fₛv/(v − vₛ)):
f₀ = (780 × 320) / (320 − 39)
f₀ = 890 Hz

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Sketch one complete cycle of a smoothly oscillating (sinusoidal) curve about the mean frequency 780 Hz: it starts at the mean value at t = 0 (the source moves tangentially, so no Doppler shift), falls to a minimum trough (source moving away), rises through the mean to a maximum peak (source moving towards), and returns to the mean value at the end of the rotation. The curve is symmetric about f = 780 Hz, with equal maximum and minimum deviations.

questions.title: Metal wire — resistivity, charge carriers & thermistor circuit

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Resistance is the potential difference per unit current (R = V/I).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Complete Fig. 6.1 using the correct circuit symbols so that the battery, the wire (drawn as a fixed resistor — a rectangle) and the thermistor (rectangle with a diagonal line through it) are all connected in series with one another.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: As the temperature of the thermistor increases, its resistance decreases (negative temperature coefficient). The total resistance of the series circuit therefore decreases, so the current increases; since P = I²R, the power dissipated in the wire increases.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Quarks: up = +⅔e, down = −⅓e, strange = −⅓e
Antiquarks (each with the opposite charge to its quark): up = −⅔e, down = +⅓e, strange = +⅓e

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Hadrons.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Baryons are composed of three quarks (or three antiquarks), whereas mesons are composed of one quark and one antiquark.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: In β⁺ decay, an up quark changes to a down quark (a proton changes into a neutron); a positron and an (electron) neutrino are emitted.
